initialize_session.title: Open an MCP session
initialize_session.description: Begin an MCP session, telling the server which protocol version and capabilities the client supports and learning the server's in return. The protocol expects this before other calls, and the server's reply is what says whether it offers tools, prompts or resources at all.

protocol_version.description: MCP protocol version the client speaks, e.g. "2025-06-18".

capabilities.description: What the client supports, as the protocol's capabilities object.

client_name.description: Name the client identifies itself by.

client_version.description: Version the client identifies itself by.

output.description: The server's JSON-RPC response, carrying its protocol version and capabilities.

result.description: protocolVersion, capabilities and serverInfo.

list_server_tools.title: List the MCP server's tools
list_server_tools.description: Ask Attio's MCP server which tools it exposes, over the protocol's tools/list method. The server decides what it offers and publishes an inputSchema for each, so this is how to discover the real CRM surface -- and the exact argument names -- before calling anything.

cursor.description: Paging cursor from a previous tools/list response.

output.description: The server's JSON-RPC response listing its tools.

result.description: `tools`, each with a name, description and inputSchema.

call_server_tool.title: Call a tool on the MCP server
call_server_tool.description: Invoke one of the Attio MCP server's tools by name. The name and the shape of `arguments` come from `list_server_tools`, not from this package -- and since the server's tools act on a live Attio portal, one of them may well create, update or delete a CRM record.

name.description: Name of the server tool to call, from list_server_tools.

arguments.description: Arguments for that tool, matching the inputSchema the server published.

result.description: `content` blocks, and `isError` when the tool itself failed.

list_server_prompts.title: List the MCP server's prompts
list_server_prompts.description: The prompt templates the server publishes, over the protocol's prompts/list method. A server that offers none answers with an empty list rather than an error.

cursor.description: Paging cursor from a previous prompts/list response.

output.description: The server's JSON-RPC response listing its prompts.

result.description: `prompts`, each with a name, description and arguments.

get_server_prompt.title: Get a prompt from the MCP server
get_server_prompt.description: Render one of the server's prompt templates with the arguments it declares, over prompts/get. Returns the messages the template expands to.

name.description: Name of the prompt, from list_server_prompts.

arguments.description: Values for the arguments that prompt declares.

result.description: `description` and the expanded `messages`.

list_server_resources.title: List the MCP server's resources
list_server_resources.description: The resources the server exposes for reading, over resources/list. On a CRM server these are typically records and record collections addressable by URI rather than by a tool call.

cursor.description: Paging cursor from a previous resources/list response.

output.description: The server's JSON-RPC response listing its resources.

result.description: `resources`, each with a uri, name and mimeType.

read_server_resource.title: Read a resource from the MCP server
read_server_resource.description: Fetch the contents of one resource by its URI, over resources/read. The URIs come from `list_server_resources`; the server decides how it addresses its own data.

uri.description: URI of the resource, from list_server_resources.

result.description: `contents`, each with a uri, mimeType and text or blob.
